To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cooperative feedback from PU to SU is a promising approach to design CB, and that the optimal tradeoff between the bit-allocation for quantization of the SU-to-PU CDI and that for quantization of IPC signal is a function of the number of SU antennas, the number of feedback bits, the PU-to-SU channel gain, and the SU transmit power.

(1) cooperative feedback/feedforward of SU CDI from PU receiver to SU transmitter can improve the SU outage probability, and the optimal tradeoff between the feedback bit-allocation for the SU-to-PU CDI and the IPC is characterized; (2) the outage probability performance can be further improved if the SU transmitter is allowed to transmit the SU CDI to the PU receiver, and a novel algorithm is proposed to achieve the optimal performance.
cooperative feedback and feedforward of the CDI and interference power control signal from the PU receiver allow for efficient CB in MISO-SISO cognitive radio systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design of a new CB algorithm for cognitive radio networks based on the PU receiver's cooperative feedback, which is a practical solution for efficient spectrum sharing in a cognitive radio environment.
the fundamental problem of how to efficiently utilize the PU's feedback for CB, which is an important issue in the practical implementation of CB in cognitive radio networks.

the practical design of cognitive beamforming based on the PU receiver's finite-rate feedback, and it offers an effective solution for the efficient spectrum sharing in cognitive radio networks with multiantenna SUs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed cooperative feedback/feedforward based CB algorithms are able to significantly enhance the SU-link performance while guaranteeing the interference to the PUs within the tolerable interference margins.
the proposed cooperative feedback/feedforward paradigm for CB is able to significantly reduce the SU transmit beamforming complexity and enhance the SU-link outage probability performance.
cooperative feedback/feedforward can significantly reduce the SU transmission outage probability compared to the non-cooperative feedback/feedforward case.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed algorithms are simple to implement, and the corresponding outage probabilities are easy to evaluate.
cooperative feedback/feedforward is an effective way for the PU to assist the SU in designing CB, which is particularly useful for a SU with limited feedback resources.
the PU's cooperative finite-rate feedback can significantly improve the performance of the SU link in a MISO-SISO cognitive network.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed cooperative feedback/feedforward paradigm can be readily implemented in practical cognitive radio networks with limited channel-state information feedback from the PU to the SU.

, by exploiting the cooperative feedback and feedforward from the PU receiver, the SU can achieve a better performance than the non-cooperative case where the SU does not receive any feedback from the PU.
the proposed cooperative feedback paradigm is a promising approach for CB design in cognitive radio networks.
